A1.justification: Both PDFs describe PhantomWiki. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable, allowing retained, revised and added material to be reliably matched.

before.justification: v1 reports original dataset-generation runtimes and LLM evaluations, including Table 2 and analyses of question difficulty, corpus size and single-answer questions.

after.justification: v2 retains original empirical evaluations and reports additional multi-hop retrieval, article-rephrasing and fine-tuning results in Section 7 and Appendix D.

M1.justification: The proposed generator retains the same family/friendship construction, random attributes, templated articles, context-free question grammar and Prolog answer generation. Rephrasing and SFT/GRPO are evaluated experimentally; they do not replace components of the proposed generation pipeline. The retriever replacement concerns evaluation baselines.

E1.justification: Coverage remains synthetic question answering about people, relationships and attributes. Appendix D.2 extends v1's preliminary article-generation check into QA evaluation on short and long LLM-rephrased corpora, adding input-style scenarios. The additional fine-tuning instances retain the existing domain and question types.

E2.justification: The main ZeroShot-RAG and CoT-RAG baselines replace UAE-LARGE-V1 retrieval with BM25. Appendix D.1 adds evaluated Self-Ask and IRCoT comparators, while Table 3 introduces comparisons between prompting, SFT and GRPO on Qwen2.5-0.5B and Qwen2.5-3B.

E3.justification: The main RAG protocol changes to BM25 while retaining top-4 retrieval; the added multi-hop comparison uses BM25/top-5. New fine-tuning protocols use 5,000 QA pairs from ten universes, full versus LoRA training, three epochs and evaluation on three held-out instances. Appendix D.2 also specifies new article-rephrasing and evaluation procedures.

E4.justification: v2 adds quantitative comparisons of templated, short-rephrased and long-rephrased articles, with an annotated factual-error example, beyond v1's preliminary hallucination observation. It also tests difficulty-dependent performance after SFT/GRPO and with multi-hop retrieval. The existing single-answer control in Figure 7 is retained, not newly introduced.

E5.justification: Table 2 newly reports three-dataset-seed means and standard errors for GPT-4o's RAG results, where v1 supplied point estimates, and narrows the stated exception to GPT-4o CoT/ReAct. The general three-seed reporting practice remains unchanged. Removing v1's sampling table also removes its explicit decoding seed of zero.

E6.justification: Table 2 replaces RAG results under changed retrieval conditions: Llama-3.3-70B CoT-RAG at n=50 changes from 20.01% with UAE to 27.63% with BM25. In-context and ReAct scores are retained. Tables 3–4 and Figures 8–10 add fine-tuning, multi-hop and article-style results. The text also corrects the small-universe winner to DeepSeek-R1-32B CoT, consistent with both versions' 52.42% entry.

T1.justification: The CFG definitions and productions in Appendices A–B, Prolog reasoning examples and complexity arguments in Section 3.3 are unchanged. The added empirical memorization discussion supplies no new theorem, proof or formal guarantee.

C1.justification: The central claims of scalable, on-demand, contamination-resistant evaluation remain. However, v1's conclusion explicitly leaves empirical testing and formal justification of memorization resistance to future work; v2 removes that reservation and states in Section 7 that its fine-tuning results demonstrate robustness to memorization.

C2.justification: Beyond v1's reasoning/retrieval discussion, v2 interprets fine-tuning through the distinction between fact memorization and learning template structure, discusses multi-branch answer-tracking failures, and motivates sparse retrieval for synthetic corpora. Its conclusion newly emphasizes limited fact/relation complexity and article realism, replacing the earlier explicit reservation about untested memorization resistance.

D1.justification: Appendix D adds rephrasing prompts and sampling settings, FlashRAG implementation information, and extensive fine-tuning details covering GPUs, libraries, optimization, batching and sequence limits. A sample-dataset access pointer and example corpus are added. Conversely, v1's default sampling table is removed, and Appendix C.2 retains an embedding-search description despite specifying BM25.

R1.justification: Section 2 substantially broadens positioning through classic QA, long-context, synthetic and dynamic benchmarks, including RepLiQA, RULER, RealTime QA and FreshQA. It revises comparisons with ToolQA and CLUTRR and acknowledges existing customizable synthetic benchmarks. New experimental citations include Self-Ask, IRCoT, LoRA and GRPO-related work.

P1.justification: The introduction replaces extended descriptions of three evaluation settings with a compact sequence of design contributions. Related work is extensively rewritten into named topic groups, and the conclusion is revised. A fine-tuning section and Software and Data section alter the narrative structure; appendix subsections and several explanations are reorganized.

P2.justification: v2 adds fine-tuning and multi-hop comparison tables and Figures 8–10, redraws the pipeline illustration, and reformats Table 2 with grouped universe-size labels. Figure 7 is relocated and its caption expanded. The old sampling-parameter Table 3 is removed; v2's Table 3 contains different, newly reported content.

improvement.justification: v2 strengthens empirical support through more suitable retrieval baselines, quantitative article-style checks and held-out fine-tuning experiments, and corrects the Table 2 ranking discussion. The gain is limited by mismatched retriever/top-k settings in the multi-hop comparison, stale embedding-search descriptions after the BM25 switch, and a memorization-resistance interpretation broader than the two-small-model study establishes. These additions provide useful validation without fully resolving the central robustness questions.
